issues.title: Cheap run-deduped BF probe + push BF into DELIM_GET-build subquery scans
issues.hypothesis: In a warm JSON profile of the current best q21 (latency 1.03s, ~7s summed CPU, so the query is CPU-bound), the two subquery INNER hash joins (lineitem probe ⋈ DELIM_SCAN build on l_orderkey = AND l_suppkey <>) are the two largest operators: l2 join 1.79s CPU over 59.99M probe rows (2.93M matches), l3 join 1.09s over 37.9M rows (1.85M matches). Their scans carry only useless min/max filters (5..59999777). E0003 pushed a BF into both scans: scan output fell to ~3.5M rows and the join to ~0.44s, but the scans' CPU rose by 0.6-0.9s each (hash + random 64-bit-sector lookup on every row), which cancelled the gain. E0004 wrote a fast path in BFTableFilter::Filter for flat, NULL-free integer keys: it hashes inline and reuses the previous result while the key equals the previous key. It had no target because no BF reached clustered keys. Together the two should work: probe keys come in runs (the table is clustered on the join key, ~4 rows per key), so the fast path removes most of the per-row hash and lookup. That leaves the join savings (~2s CPU) while cutting the scan penalty (~1.5s) by a factor of 3-4.
issues.plan: Three parts in one diff. (1) src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp GenerateJoinFilters, around lines 302-309: when join.children[1] is LOGICAL_DELIM_GET, set build_side_has_filter = true. A DELIM_GET carries the distinct keys of an already-filtered outer side. Keep the existing probe > build cardinality check. (2) src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (line ~775): replace `ht->conditions.size() == 1` with `ht->equality_predicate_columns.size() == 1` and keep the `cmp == COMPARE_EQUAL` requirement. Equalities are ordered first, so conditions[0] is the equality that PushBloomFilter uses. (3) src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp BFTableFilter::Filter: add a fast path when keys_v is FLAT, has no NULLs in the approved rows, and has an integer physical type (INT8..INT64, UINT8..UINT64). Walk the approved rows (through sel if set). Keep prev_key and prev_found. When key != prev_key, compute duckdb::Hash<T>(key), the same function VectorOperations::Hash uses, and call filter.LookupOne. Write survivors directly into sel and approved_tuple_count. Any other input uses the existing path. Check with a JSON profile that both l2 and l3 scans show `IN BF(l_orderkey)` and that scan CPU stays under ~0.5s each.
issues.expected_gain: q21: -8% to -15%. Join CPU falls by ~2s, scan CPU rises by ~0.4s instead of ~1.5s, out of ~7s total CPU.
issues.generality: Any correlated EXISTS/NOT EXISTS or IN subquery that is decorrelated into a delim join whose inner side scans a large table on the correlation key. Also any hash join with one equality plus residual non-equality conditions. The fast path helps every BF probe on integer keys that come in sorted or clustered runs (fact tables ordered by a foreign key). It could get slower: BF probes on unique or random integer keys pay one extra compare per row (negligible), and DELIM_GET builds that filter nothing get a BF they don't need. The probe > build cardinality gate limits that case.
issues.risk: Low to medium. Correctness: the BF is optional, and for NULL-free integer keys the inline hash must match VectorOperations::Hash exactly, so use duckdb::Hash<T>. Fall back for any vector with NULLs or that is not flat. Performance risk: the gain may still be under the 5% bar, since parts 1-2 alone gave 0%.

issues.title: Hash join probe: reuse hash/bucket for consecutive equal integer probe keys
issues.hypothesis: If the BF route fails: the l2 and l3 subquery joins spend ~30ns per probe row (1.79s / 60M rows) on a 735K-entry pointer table that does not fit in cache. Probe keys come in runs of ~4 equal values, so 3/4 of the hashes and pointer-table misses repeat the previous row's work.
issues.plan: In JoinHashTable probe (src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp, the hash and GetRowPointers path), for a single flat, NULL-free integer key column, compute the hash once per run and copy the bucket pointer or salt result to the following equal keys. Verify the function names before implementing.
issues.expected_gain: q21: -5% to -10%, if the probe is dominated by cache misses on the pointer table.
issues.generality: Hash joins probed by clustered or sorted foreign keys. Unique or random keys pay one compare per row.
issues.risk: Medium. The probe code is intricate: salts, chains, and residual non-equality predicates.

output.memory:
## Planner memory (q21 specialisation run)

## Tooling facts
- dbe-tool profile / sql output is truncated (~150 lines / by width). Bash cat/ls happened to work in round 5, but prefer Read/Grep.
- **Every `dbe-tool sql` call is a FRESH PROCESS with a cold buffer pool.** Warm up in the same call first.
- Full warm profile recipe (works): one sql call with `CREATE TEMP TABLE w AS <q>; CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE w AS <q>; PRAGMA enable_profiling='json';
  SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/p.json'; CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE w AS <q>; PRAGMA disable_profiling;`
  Then a second call: `SELECT string_agg(trim(line),' ') FROM (SELECT unnest(string_split(content, chr(10))) line FROM read_text('<path>')) WHERE line SIMILAR TO
  '.*(operator_name|operator_timing|operator_cardinality|"latency|Filters|Join Type|Conditions|Table).*'` piped through `fold -w 250` (one row, so no truncation).
- Shell variables and `$(...)` are blocked. `EXPLAIN (FORMAT json)` times out. Operator timings are summed CPU across threads; latency is wall time.

## Warm facts, CURRENT BEST (verified round 5, SF10, 8 threads)
- Latency ~1.03s, ~7s summed CPU, so q21 is CPU-bound: CPU/8 ≈ 0.87s.
- Operator CPU: l1 scan 0.35 (min/max only) + FILTER 0.125 + suppkey join 0.28; orders scan 0.34 (status='F' + BF(l_orderkey));
  orders⋈l1 join 0.37; RIGHT_DELIM 0.25; LEFT_DELIM 0.12;
  **l2 subquery INNER join 1.79s** (60M probe rows → 2.93M), l2 scan 0.33 (min/max only, NO BF);
  RIGHT_SEMI join 0.41; **l3 INNER join 1.09s** (37.9M probe → 1.85M), l3 scan 0.35 + FILTER 0.13 (NO BF); ANTI join 0.35;
  delim HASH_GROUP_BYs 0.04-0.06.
- The only BF in the current best is on the orders scan (unique keys).
- lineitem is clustered by l_orderkey (~4 rows per key). lineitem cols are BitPacking.

## Codebase facts
- Optimizer order: BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE (optimizer.cpp:247) before JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN (:320).
- GenerateJoinFilters (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp): build_side_has_filter is set at :302-309. For a DELIM_GET rhs it uses IsFiltering(children[0]).
  It skips LEFT/OUTER/ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI/RIGHT_SEMI/MARK/SINGLE. The q21 subquery joins are INNER (lineitem probe ⋈ DELIM_SCAN build).
- BF gate: CanUseBloomFilter physical_hash_join.cpp:761 (`ht->conditions.size()==1` at :775). BF impl: src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp
  (BFTableFilter::Filter :96 → HashInternal → LookupHashes; one 64-bit sector per key). Scan dispatch: column_segment.cpp:558.
- Optional min/max filters are zonemap-only. The optional BF is evaluated per row.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp, MAX_BUILD_SIZE 1,048,576.

## History
- E0001 RETIRED: BF for 1 equality + non-eq conds, DELIM_GET build → official ~0% (local -4..-7%).
- E0002 RETIRED: BF for sparse perfect HJ (l1 suppkey): the BF hashing cost exceeds the savings on a cheap scan.
- E0003 RETIRED: BF on l2/l3 scans: rows 60M→3.5M, joins → ~0.44s, but scan CPU +0.6-0.9s each → 0%.
- E0004 RETIRED: BF run-dedupe fast path (bloom_filter.cpp): implementation worked, but no BF on clustered keys in the current best → no target.
  This failed on a stale premise, not because the idea was bad.
- Round 5: dispatched the E0003+E0004 combination (push BF into the DELIM_GET-build subquery scans AND run-dedupe the probe).
  If it gives ~0% again, the BF route is exhausted for q21; switch to the hash-join probe run-dedupe issue (backlog) or restructure the subquery joins.

## Ideas for later
- Hash join probe run-dedupe for clustered integer keys (filed as an issue): l2/l3 joins cost ~30ns per probe row.
- Exact bitmap filter for dense integer key sets (bit test at key-min, no hash) when the build key range is < ~64x the key count.
- Big/risky: rewrite EXISTS/NOT EXISTS (k= AND s<>) as per-key aggregates (count distinct suppkey per orderkey); share the l2/l3 scans.
